svg.title: Queue pop and requeue control flow
svg.desc: Own-list search bypasses queues. Private discovery prioritizes big, then ordinary when unrestricted. Shared discovery follows if no victim. Private requeue can precede scanning.

g.text: When does consume() happen?
pgbuf_get_victim(): stop as soon as a search returns a victim.
1 Own-private search, if eligible: direct list lookup. NO QUEUE POP.
no victim
2 Private helper only if quota enabled AND flush daemon available
Try BIG-private consume first
empty + restricted? return NULL
empty
Try ORDINARY-private consume
only when unrestricted
If either supplies an index: N > 100 AND N > 2Q AND C > 1?
Try big requeue BEFORE scan. Success means no second publication.
Otherwise: scan, then try ordinary requeue if C > 0 AND N > Q.
skipped / no victim
3 Shared helper: try SHARED consume, then scan that list
No flush daemon + failed scan + C > 0: scan the same list once more.
Requeue if C > 0 AND (has_flush_thread OR victim found).
N = list length; Q = quota; C = candidate count at each decision.
No successful requeue → clear registration flag. A pop may find no victim.
f799e05 source trace; shared outer-loop bounds are explained beside this diagram.
